label: Saves what people create
question: Will the app save things people create, like posts, bookings or profiles?
why: Saving anything between visits needs a database.
not_sure_note: Most apps save something. If yours does, it needs a database.

label: People log in
question: Will people create accounts and log in?
why: Accounts need a login service and a place to store each person's data.
not_sure_note: If people ever see their own data, they need to log in.

label: People pay you
question: Will people pay you inside the app?
why: Taking money needs a payment provider and changes which free plans you can use.
not_sure_note: Charging later is common. Some free hosting plans forbid commercial use, so it is worth knowing early.

label: People upload files
question: Will people upload photos, videos or files?
why: Uploads need file storage, which is separate from the database.
not_sure_note: Profile pictures count. If people upload anything, you need file storage.

label: Big uploads
question: Will uploads include videos or files bigger than a few megabytes?
why: Big files can break when they pass through a server with size and time limits.
not_sure_note: Phone videos are usually big. Plan for direct uploads if videos are possible.

label: Live updates
question: Should people see changes instantly without refreshing, like chat or a live feed?
why: Live updates need a host that holds connections open or a database that pushes changes.
not_sure_note: Without live updates, people refresh to see changes. That is fine for most apps.

label: Long-running jobs
question: Will the app do anything that takes more than a minute, like processing video or a big AI task?
why: Many hosts cut off requests after a time limit.
not_sure_note: Most app actions finish in seconds. Video processing and big AI jobs are the usual exceptions.

label: Scheduled tasks
question: Does anything need to happen on a schedule, like a daily email or a nightly cleanup?
why: Scheduled work needs a host or service that can run code on a timer.
not_sure_note: Reminder emails and weekly summaries are scheduled tasks.

label: Sends email
question: Will the app send emails, like confirmations, receipts or reminders?
why: Sending email from an app needs an email service and a verified domain.
not_sure_note: Receipts, invites and password resets all count. Most apps with accounts send some email.

label: Has its own web address
question: Do you want your own web address, like yourapp.com?
why: Every host gives you a free address like yourapp.vercel.app. Your own domain costs a yearly fee, and you need one to send email from your app's name.
not_sure_note: You can launch on your host's free address and buy a domain later. Sending email from your app's name needs one.

label: AI features
question: Will the app use AI, like a chatbot or generating text or images?
why: AI features need a model provider and a server to keep the API key private.
not_sure_note: AI can be added later without changing the rest of the stack, as long as you have server code.

label: Pulls data from other websites
question: Will the app pull information from other websites, like prices, listings or articles?
why: Reading other websites needs a scraper or that site's official API, and each site's terms decide what you're allowed to collect.
not_sure_note: If what you show comes from websites you don't run, plan for a scraper or that site's official API.

label: Phone app, now or later
question: Will there be an iPhone or Android app, now or later?
why: Some services work in phone apps and some do not, so choosing now avoids a rebuild.
not_sure_note: If a phone app is possible, prefer services with mobile SDKs. It costs nothing now.

label: Tracks how people use it
question: Do you want to see how many people visit and what they use?
why: Counting visitors and actions needs an analytics tool, and the tool you pick decides whether you need a cookie banner.
not_sure_note: Most launched apps add analytics to see what people actually use. It's quick to add later.

label: Alerts when something breaks
question: Do you want an alert when the app breaks for someone?
why: Errors in a live app happen on other people's devices, where you can't see them. A monitoring tool records them and tells you.
not_sure_note: Before real people use the app, error alerts mean you hear about problems before someone complains.

label: Connects to other tools
question: Should the app kick off work in other tools, like posting to Slack, updating a spreadsheet or syncing a CRM?
why: Hooking an app to other tools is often quicker with an automation service than with code, and each one prices by how many steps run.
not_sure_note: If you later want the app to notify a team or update another tool, an automation service can do it without new code in the app.

label: Uses another service's data
question: Will the app show data from another service's API, like sports scores, weather or maps?
why: Data from someone else's API comes with their rules: a key to keep private, limits on how often you can ask, and sometimes no promise it won't change.
not_sure_note: If what you show comes from another company's service, plan where the key lives and what happens when their API is slow or down.
